source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: All 66 selected original verse records bind exactly once to matching public verse labels. No record partition or offset in this scope. Titles remain inside their verse labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain title as name with vocabulary rather than identify beyond source.
verses.before: The words of Qoheleth, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.after: The words of Qohelet, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of Qoheleth, son of David, king in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated hevel metaphor; note transience and elusiveness.
verses.before: Vapor of vapors, says Qoheleth, vapor of vapors—everything is vapor.
verses.after: “Breath of breaths,” says Qohelet, “breath of breaths! Everything is a breath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Vapor of vapors, says Qoheleth, vapor of vapors—everything is vapor.

verses.rationale: Preserve gain, toil repetition, and recurring perspective.
verses.before: What gain does a person have from all their labor in which they labor under the sun?
verses.after: What gain does a person have from all the toil he toils at under the sun?
verses.tsw_comparator: What gain does a person have from all their labor in which they labor under the sun?

verses.rationale: Keep human/earth duration contrast.
verses.before: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever.
verses.after: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth stands through the ages.
verses.tsw_comparator: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever.

verses.rationale: Retain weary sun image.
verses.before: The sun rises, and the sun sets; it hurries to its place, and there it rises.
verses.after: The sun rises, and the sun sets; it pants back to the place where it rises.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sun rises, and the sun sets; it hurries to its place, and there it rises.

verses.rationale: Preserve directional cycle and repetition.
verses.before: Going toward the south, and turning toward the north, turning, turning goes the wind; and upon its circuits the wind returns.
verses.after: The wind goes south and circles north; round and round it goes, returning on its circuits.
verses.tsw_comparator: Going toward the south, and turning toward the north, turning, turning goes the wind; and upon its circuits the wind returns.

verses.rationale: Do not insert a modern water-cycle explanation.
verses.before: All the streams go to the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the streams go, there they return to go again.
verses.after: All streams flow to the sea, but the sea is never full. To the place where the streams flow, there they flow again.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the streams go to the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the streams go, there they return to go again.

verses.rationale: Retain things/words ambiguity and unsatisfied senses.
verses.before: Everything are weary; no one can speak of them. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor is the ear filled with hearing.
verses.after: All things are wearisome, more than anyone can express. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.tsw_comparator: All things are weary; no one can speak of them. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor is the ear filled with hearing.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated cyclical claims.
verses.before: What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; there is nothing new under the sun.
verses.after: What has been is what will be; what has been done is what will be done. There is nothing new under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; there is nothing new under the sun.

verses.rationale: Retain question and temporal rebuttal.
verses.before: Is there anything of which one says, “Look—this is new”? It has already been in ages before us.
verses.after: Is there something of which one can say, “Look, this is new”? It already existed in ages before us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there anything of which one says, “Look—this is new”? It has already been in ages before us.

verses.rationale: Choose people referent while noting former/later things possible.
verses.before: There is no remembrance of the former ones, nor will there be remembrance of the later ones to come among people who come afterward.
verses.after: There is no remembrance of those who came before; even those yet to come will not be remembered by those who come afterward.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no remembrance of the former ones, nor will there be remembrance of the later ones to come among those who come afterward.

verses.rationale: Preserve past royal self-presentation.
verses.before: I, Qoheleth, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.after: I, Qohelet, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Qoheleth, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep heavens distinct from sun and difficult divine gift.
verses.before: I gave my heart to seek and to explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. It is a grievous task that God has given to human beings to occupy them.
verses.after: I set my heart to seek and investigate with wisdom everything done under the heavens. It is a grievous task that God has given humankind to occupy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave my heart to seek and to explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. It is a grievous task that God has given to human beings to occupy them.

verses.rationale: Retain hevel and impossible shepherding image.
verses.before: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and see: everything is vapor and a chasing after wind.
verses.after: I saw all the deeds done under the sun. Look: everything is a breath, a herding of wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun, and see: everything is vapor and a chasing after wind.

verses.rationale: Keep two limits without moralizing their causes.
verses.before: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
verses.after: What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is missing cannot be counted.
verses.tsw_comparator: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

verses.rationale: Preserve comparative royal claim and heart’s experience.
verses.before: I spoke with my heart, saying, “Look, I have grown great and increased in wisdom beyond everyone who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.”
verses.after: I said to myself, “Look, I have grown in wisdom beyond everyone who was over Jerusalem before me. My heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I spoke with my heart, saying, “Look, I have grown great and increased in wisdom beyond all who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.”

verses.rationale: Keep opposed fields of inquiry.
verses.before: I gave my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I knew that this too is a pursuit of wind.
verses.after: I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I learned that this too is a herding of wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I knew that this too is a pursuit of wind.

verses.rationale: Preserve troubling wisdom/pain connection.
verses.before: For with much wisdom comes much vexation, and one who increases knowledge increases pain.
verses.after: For with much wisdom comes much frustration; whoever adds knowledge adds pain.
verses.tsw_comparator: For with much wisdom comes much vexation, and one who increases knowledge increases pain.

verses.rationale: Keep self-addressed experiment and verdict.
verses.before: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; see what is good.” But look: this too was vapor.
verses.after: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure. Enjoy what is good!” But look, this too was a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; see what is good.” But look: this too was vapor.

verses.rationale: Retain questions rather than flatten all pleasure into evil.
verses.before: Of laughter I said, “Madness!” And of pleasure, “What does this accomplish?”
verses.after: Of laughter I said, “Madness!” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Of laughter I said, “Madness!” And of pleasure, “What does this accomplish?”

verses.rationale: Preserve tension of wine, wisdom, and experimental folly.
verses.before: I searched in my heart how to draw my body along with wine—while my heart was guiding me with wisdom—and how to grasp folly, until I might see what is good for human beings to do under heaven during the number of the days of their lives.
verses.after: I explored in my heart how to draw my body along with wine—while my heart still guided me with wisdom—and how to take hold of folly, until I could see what was good for people to do under the heavens during their few days of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: I searched in my heart how to draw my body along with wine—while my heart was guiding me with wisdom—and how to grasp folly, until I might see what is good for human beings to do under heaven during the number of the days of their lives.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated for myself.
verses.before: I made my works great. I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
verses.after: I made my works great. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself.
verses.tsw_comparator: I made my works great. I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.

verses.rationale: Retain distinct cultivated spaces.
verses.before: I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every kind of fruit tree.
verses.after: I made gardens and parks for myself and planted every kind of fruit tree in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every kind of fruit tree.

verses.rationale: Keep irrigation infrastructure.
verses.before: I made pools of water for myself, to water from them a forest growing trees.
verses.after: I made pools of water for myself to irrigate a forest of growing trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: I made pools of water for myself, to water from them a forest growing trees.

verses.rationale: Preserve enslavement, birth status, and comparative claim.
verses.before: I acquired male slaves and female slaves, and household-born slaves belonged to me. I also had livestock—herds and flocks—more than everyone who were before me in Jerusalem.
verses.after: I bought male and female slaves, and I had slaves born in my household. I also possessed more cattle and flocks than anyone before me in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: I acquired male slaves and female slaves, and household-born slaves belonged to me. I also had livestock—herds and flocks—more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Choose concubines for rare shiddah; flag uncertain meaning.
verses.before: I also gathered for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I provided for myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of human beings: a consort and consorts.
verses.after: I gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and human delights—concubines in abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also gathered for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I provided for myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of human beings: a consort and consorts.

verses.rationale: Preserve retained wisdom amid excess.
verses.before: So I became great and increased beyond everyone who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.
verses.after: I became great and surpassed everyone before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also stayed with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I became great and increased beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.

verses.rationale: Keep portion distinct from lasting gain.
verses.before: Whatever my eyes asked for, I did not withhold from them. I did not keep my heart from any pleasure, for my heart rejoiced in all my labor; and this was my portion from all my labor.
verses.after: I denied my eyes nothing they asked for. I withheld no pleasure from my heart, for my heart rejoiced in all my toil. This was my portion from all my toil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever my eyes asked for, I did not withhold from them. I did not keep my heart from any pleasure, for my heart rejoiced in all my labor; and this was my portion from all my labor.

verses.rationale: Preserve reflective turn and refrain.
verses.before: Then I turned to all the works my hands had made and to the labor I had labored to do. And look: all was vapor and a chasing after wind; there was no advantage under the sun.
verses.after: Then I turned to all the work my hands had done and the toil I had spent doing it. Look: everything was a breath, a herding of wind. There was no gain under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I turned to all the works my hands had made and to the labor I had labored to do. And look: all was vapor and a chasing after wind; there was no advantage under the sun.

verses.rationale: Retain difficult successor question without naming king.
verses.before: Then I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly. For what can the one who comes after the king do, except what has already been done?
verses.after: Then I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly. For what can the person who comes after the king do, except what has already been done?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly. For what can the one who comes after the king do, except what has already been done?

verses.rationale: Keep genuine relative advantage despite prior frustration.
verses.before: I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness.
verses.after: I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, just as light has an advantage over darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness.

verses.rationale: Retain concrete proverb followed by its limit.
verses.before: The wise have their eyes in their head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also knew that one fate comes to them all.
verses.after: The wise have eyes in their heads; the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also knew that one fate meets them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wise have their eyes in their head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also knew that one fate comes to them all.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated inward speech and question.
verses.before: Then I said in my heart, “What happens to the fool will happen to me also. Why then have I become wiser?” And I said in my heart that this too is vapor.
verses.after: I said in my heart, “The fool’s fate will meet me too. Why, then, have I been so very wise?” And I said in my heart, “This too is a breath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said in my heart, “What happens to the fool will happen to me also. Why then have I become wiser?” And I said in my heart that this too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep protest rather than smooth into detached observation.
verses.before: For there is no enduring remembrance of the wise alongside the fool, since in the days to come all is already forgotten. And how the wise dies along with the fool!
verses.after: For the wise, like the fool, have no lasting remembrance. In the days to come, everything will already be forgotten. How can the wise die just like the fool?
verses.tsw_comparator: For there is no enduring remembrance of the wise alongside the fool, since in the days to come all is already forgotten. And how the wise dies along with the fool!

verses.rationale: Retain real despair in speaker’s voice.
verses.before: So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was grievous to me. For all is vapor and a chasing after wind.
verses.after: So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was grievous to me. Everything is a breath, a herding of wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was grievous to me. For all is vapor and a chasing after wind.

verses.rationale: Keep toil repetition and forced relinquishment.
verses.before: I hated all my labor at which I had labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the one who will come after me.
verses.after: I hated all the toil I had toiled at under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hated all my labor at which I had labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the one who will come after me.

verses.rationale: Retain successor uncertainty and control.
verses.before: And who knows whether that one will be wise or foolish? Yet that one will rule over all my labor, for which I labored and used wisdom under the sun. This too is vapor.
verses.after: Who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet he will control all the toil I carried out with wisdom under the sun. This too is a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: And who knows whether that one will be wise or foolish? Yet that one will rule over all my labor, for which I labored and used wisdom under the sun. This too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Preserve despair without inserted consolation.
verses.before: So I turned to give my heart over to despair concerning all the labor at which I had labored under the sun.
verses.after: So I turned toward despair in my heart over all the toil I had toiled at under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I turned to give my heart over to despair concerning all the labor at which I had labored under the sun.

verses.rationale: Keep unearned inheritance and strong evaluative evil.
verses.before: For there is a person whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, yet that person must give their portion to one who has not labored for it. This too is vapor and a great evil.
verses.after: Someone may toil with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, then leave his portion to a person who did not toil for it. This too is a breath and a great wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there is a person whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, yet that person must give their portion to one who has not labored for it. This too is vapor and a great evil.

verses.rationale: Retain gain question’s emotional dimension.
verses.before: For what does a person have from all their labor and from the striving of their heart, with which they labor under the sun?
verses.after: What does a person get from all his toil and the striving of his heart as he toils under the sun?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what does a person have from all their labor and from the striving of their heart, with which they labor under the sun?

verses.rationale: Keep sleepless heart image.
verses.before: For all their days are pains, and their task is vexation; even at night their heart does not lie down. This too is vapor.
verses.after: All his days are pain, and his occupation is frustration. Even at night his heart does not lie down. This too is a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all their days are pains, and their task is vexation; even at night their heart does not lie down. This too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Choose comparative ellipsis; note not-in-human-control alternative.
verses.before: There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and show their life what is good in their labor. This too, I saw, is from the hand of God.
verses.after: There is nothing better for a person than to eat, drink, and let himself enjoy good in his toil. This too, I saw, comes from the hand of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and show their life what is good in their labor. This too, I saw, is from the hand of God.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned first-person me; note consequential pronoun alternative.
verses.before: For who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from me?
verses.after: For who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from me?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from me?

verses.rationale: Retain both gifts/tasks and unsettling final verdict.
verses.before: For to the person who is good before him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and collecting, to give to the one who is good before God. This too is vapor and a chasing after wind.
verses.after: To the person who is good before him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy. To the sinner he gives the task of gathering and collecting, only to give it to the one who is good before God. This too is a breath, a herding of wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: For to the person who is good before him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and collecting, to give to the one who is good before God. This too is vapor and a chasing after wind.

verses.rationale: Preserve temporal frame and heavens.
verses.before: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under the heavens.
verses.after: For everything there is a season, a time for every activity under the heavens:
verses.tsw_comparator: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under the heavens.

verses.rationale: Follow active birth infinitive and paired plants.
verses.before: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot what is planted;
verses.after: a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted;
verses.tsw_comparator: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot what is planted;

verses.rationale: Retain killing without euphemism or added endorsement.
verses.before: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build;
verses.after: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build;
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build;

verses.rationale: Preserve four embodied responses.
verses.before: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.after: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance;
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.rationale: Keep unresolved stone imagery.
verses.before: a time to throw stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.after: a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to stay away from embracing;
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to throw stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

verses.rationale: Retain lose rather than only stop searching.
verses.before: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;
verses.after: a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away;
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to throw away;

verses.rationale: Keep textile and speech pairs.
verses.before: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to be silent, and a time to speak;
verses.after: a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak;
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to be silent, and a time to speak;

verses.rationale: Preserve disturbing hate and war pairings.
verses.before: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
verses.after: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.

verses.rationale: Resume gain question after time poem.
verses.before: What gain is there for the one who works in what they labor at?
verses.after: What gain does the worker have from his toil?
verses.tsw_comparator: What gain is there for the one who works in what they labor at?

verses.rationale: Retain divine assignment.
verses.before: I have seen the task that God has given to human beings to occupy them.
verses.after: I have seen the task God has given humankind to occupy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have seen the task that God has given to human beings to occupy them.

verses.rationale: Keep olam and limit of human comprehension; note duration ambiguity.
verses.before: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put eternity in their hearts, yet without enabling anyone to find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.
verses.after: He has made everything fitting in its time. He has also put eternity in their hearts, yet humans cannot discover the work God has done from beginning to end.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put eternity in their hearts, yet without enabling anyone to find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.

verses.rationale: Preserve do good rather than silently substitute feel good.
verses.before: I know that there is nothing good for them except to rejoice and to do good during their lives.
verses.after: I know there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good during their lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know that there is nothing good for them except to rejoice and to do good during their lives.

verses.rationale: Keep ordinary enjoyment and divine gift.
verses.before: And also, whenever anyone eats and drinks and sees good in all their labor, this is God’s gift.
verses.after: Moreover, when anyone eats, drinks, and enjoys good in all his toil, this is God’s gift.
verses.tsw_comparator: And also, whenever anyone eats and drinks and sees good in all their labor, this is God’s gift.

verses.rationale: Retain permanence, limits, and fear.
verses.before: I know that whatever God does will be forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it. God has done it so that people may fear before him.
verses.after: I know that everything God does endures forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it. God has acted so that people will fear before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know that whatever God does will be forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it. God has done it so that people may fear before him.

verses.rationale: Preserve pursued/driven-away ambiguity rather than erase into cyclic slogan.
verses.before: What has been already is, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks what has been pursued.
verses.after: What is has already been; what will be has already been. And God seeks what has been driven away.
verses.tsw_comparator: What has been already is, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks what has been pursued.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated there and institutional injustice.
verses.before: And further, I saw under the sun: in the place of justice, there was wickedness; and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.
verses.after: I saw something else under the sun: in the place of judgment, wickedness was there; in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.
verses.tsw_comparator: And further, I saw under the sun: in the place of justice, there was wickedness; and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.

verses.rationale: Retain difficult there without inventing location.
verses.before: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and for every deed there.”
verses.after: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every activity and for every deed there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and for every deed there.”

verses.rationale: Keep unsettling human-animal comparison and divine testing.
verses.before: I said in my heart concerning human beings: God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are animals.
verses.after: I said in my heart concerning human beings, “God is testing them, so they may see that they themselves are animals.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said in my heart concerning human beings: God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are animals.

verses.rationale: Retain shared breath and death without doctrinal qualification.
verses.before: For the fate of human beings and the fate of animals is one fate for them: as one dies, so dies the other; and one breath belongs to all. Human beings have no advantage over animals, for all is vapor.
verses.after: For humans have a fate and animals have a fate; one fate belongs to them both. As one dies, so does the other. They all have one breath, and humans have no advantage over animals, for everything is a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the fate of human beings and the fate of animals is one fate for them: as one dies, so dies the other; and one breath belongs to all. Human beings have no advantage over animals, for all is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep threefold all and dust refrain.
verses.before: All go to one place. All came from the dust, and all return to the dust.
verses.after: All go to one place. All came from dust, and all return to dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: All go to one place. All came from the dust, and all return to the dust.

verses.rationale: Preserve epistemic question rather than assert an answer.
verses.before: Who knows whether the spirit of human beings goes upward, and whether the spirit of the animal goes down to the earth?
verses.after: Who knows whether the human spirit rises upward and the animal’s spirit goes downward to the earth?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who knows whether the spirit of human beings goes upward, and whether the spirit of the animal goes down to the earth?

verses.rationale: Keep portion and future-knowledge question.
verses.before: So I saw that there is nothing better than for people to rejoice in their work, for that is their portion. For who can bring them to see what will be after them?
verses.after: So I saw that there is nothing better than for a person to rejoice in his work, for that is his portion. Who can bring him to see what will come after him?
